subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Measuring development and the development gap
Resource issues and reducing the gap

options: The average income per person in a country
questions.explain: Gross National Income per capita is a common economic development indicator.
HDI is a composite measure of development across health, education and income.

options: A high GNI per capita and high HDI
questions.explain: HICs have higher incomes and development levels than LICs.

options: The difference in development between richer and poorer countries
questions.explain: The development gap describes inequality between HICs and LICs.

questions.q: A single indicator like GNI per capita can be misleading because it:
options: Is an average and hides inequalities within a country
questions.explain: Averages mask internal inequality, so several indicators are used together.

questions.q: As a country develops, its birth and death rates usually:
questions.explain: The demographic transition sees death rates then birth rates fall with development.

questions.q: A historical cause of uneven development in many countries was:
options: Colonialism, which exploited resources and shaped economies
questions.explain: Colonial exploitation is one physical, economic and historical cause of the development gap.

questions.q: Life expectancy is a development indicator that measures:
options: The average age people are expected to live to
questions.explain: Higher life expectancy generally indicates better healthcare and living standards.

options: Give producers in poorer countries a fairer, guaranteed price
questions.explain: Fair trade improves incomes and conditions for producers in LICs.

options: Technology suited to local skills, resources and needs
questions.explain: Appropriate technology is affordable and sustainable for local communities.

options: Freeing up money that a country can invest in services
questions.explain: Cancelling or reducing debt allows spending on health, education and infrastructure.

options: Having a reliable and affordable supply of a resource
questions.explain: Security means dependable access; insecurity causes shortages and conflict.

questions.q: Short-term emergency aid is best suited to:
options: Responding to disasters such as earthquakes or famine
questions.explain: Emergency aid provides immediate relief; long-term aid supports development.

questions.q: A country wants sustainable, long-term development rather than dependency. A suitable strategy is:
options: Investing in education and appropriate technology
Relying only on emergency food aid
questions.explain: Long-term strategies build local capacity and reduce dependency.

questions.q: Two countries have the same GNI per capita but very different HDI values. This shows that:
options: Income alone does not fully measure development
questions.explain: Differences in health and education can produce different HDI despite similar income.

questions.q: Increasing trade (rather than aid) can help development because it:
options: Can create jobs and generate income over the long term
questions.explain: Trade can drive sustainable growth, though terms of trade matter.
